string.name: guide_subtitle
string.value: Getting started with the three streaming modes, what each option does, and FAQ

string.name: guide_prepare_title
string.value: Before you start

string.name: guide_prepare_intro
string.value: SysDVR is an open-source streaming sysmodule for the device by exelix11. This app is its HarmonyOS client, so SysDVR must be installed on your device first.

string.name: guide_prepare_step1
string.value: Install SysDVR on your device (follow the project page to install the sysmodule and the SysDVR Settings app; version 6.0 or later recommended)

string.name: guide_prepare_step2
string.value: Open SysDVR Settings, choose a streaming mode (TCP Bridge, USB or RTSP) and apply it

string.name: guide_prepare_step3
string.value: Launch a game that supports video capture (some games and system menus block recording, so there will be no picture)

string.name: guide_prepare_step4
string.value: In this app, pick the same mode as on the device and connect

string.name: guide_prepare_tip
string.value: The mode on the device must match the one selected here. After switching modes, restarting the game is recommended.

string.name: guide_tcp_title
string.value: TCP Bridge (Wi-Fi, recommended)

string.name: guide_tcp_intro
string.value: Video and audio travel over two TCP connections, with NAL replay (static scenes don't resend keyframes) and auto discovery. It's bandwidth-efficient and stable — the recommended wireless mode.

string.name: guide_tcp_step1
string.value: Put the device and your phone on the same network. Recommended: turn on “Device hotspot” on the Settings tab, tap “Hotspot settings” to see the network name and password, then join it from System Settings → Internet on the device

string.name: guide_tcp_step2
string.value: Back on the Stream tab, tap “Connect” once your device appears under “Devices on your network”. If it doesn't show up, enter the device's IP manually

string.name: guide_tcp_step3
string.value: Playback starts full screen in landscape. Tap the picture to show or hide the controls; use “Settings” at the top right to adjust sound, smoothing and more at any time

string.name: guide_tcp_item1_title
string.value: Why use the device hotspot

string.name: guide_tcp_item1_body
string.value: On 5 GHz the device only supports channels 36–48, so it can't join many phone hotspots and routers that default to other channels, and 2.4 GHz is so congested that we measured only a dozen or so fps. The device hotspot uses Wi-Fi Direct to create a 5 GHz network (channels 36–48, WPA2), so the device connects straight to your phone without a router — a steady 30 fps in our tests.

string.name: guide_tcp_item2_title
string.value: Don't join another Wi-Fi at the same time

string.name: guide_tcp_item2_body
string.value: If your phone runs the hotspot while also connected to another Wi-Fi network, the radio keeps hopping between two channels, causing periodic frame drops and audio gaps. Keep WLAN itself on — turning it off also shuts down the hotspot.

string.name: guide_tcp_tip
string.value: When using a router, put both the phone and the device on 5 GHz and avoid guest networks (they usually isolate devices, so discovery fails).

string.name: guide_usb_title
string.value: USB (cable)

string.name: guide_usb_intro
string.value: Your phone or tablet acts as the USB host and reads the stream directly from the device — no Wi-Fi interference and more consistent latency.

string.name: guide_usb_step1
string.value: Set SysDVR to USB mode on the device and use handheld mode (not docked)

string.name: guide_usb_step2
string.value: Connect the device's bottom USB-C port to your phone using an OTG adapter (USB-C male → USB-A female on the phone side) and a USB-A to USB-C cable

string.name: guide_usb_step3
string.value: Select “USB” in this app. When the device is detected below, tap “Connect” and allow access to the USB device in the system prompt

string.name: guide_usb_step4
string.value: Optionally tap “Read device info” first to check the SysDVR version, protocol and transfer method

string.name: guide_usb_item1_title
string.value: Device not detected

string.name: guide_usb_item1_body
string.value: With a C-to-C cable the phone is negotiated as the USB device (the device becomes the host), so the app sees no external device — and that doesn't change even if the phone later powers the device. Use an OTG adapter (USB-C male → USB-A female on the phone side) plus a USB-A to USB-C cable so the phone becomes the USB host. “Diagnostics” in the USB card lists the devices the system detects.

string.name: guide_usb_item2_title
string.value: Transfer method

string.name: guide_usb_item2_body
string.value: The app first tries to access the USB device directly (better performance). If the system doesn't allow that, it automatically switches to compatibility mode through the system USB service — same features, slightly higher CPU usage.

string.name: guide_usb_tip
string.value: Over USB your phone also powers the device, so keep an eye on the battery.

string.name: guide_rtsp_title
string.value: RTSP (standard protocol)

string.name: guide_rtsp_intro
string.value: The device runs a standard RTSP server (rtsp://IP:6666/) and this app plays it with ijkplayer. Broad compatibility, but no NAL replay, more bandwidth and slightly higher latency.

string.name: guide_rtsp_step1
string.value: Set SysDVR to RTSP mode on the device and note the device's IP shown in SysDVR Settings

string.name: guide_rtsp_step2
string.value: Select “RTSP” in this app, enter the IP below and tap “Connect”. If it fails, tap “Test connection” to see why

string.name: guide_rtsp_item1_title
string.value: Differences from other modes

string.name: guide_rtsp_item1_body
string.value: In RTSP mode the device doesn't broadcast, so you must enter the IP manually. Smoothing, background keep-alive and turning off the device screen are unavailable. Streaming pauses in the background and reconnects automatically when you return.

string.name: guide_rtsp_item2_title
string.value: Stuck on “Connecting” or “Connection lost”

string.name: guide_rtsp_item2_body
string.value: SysDVR's RTSP server accepts only one connection at a time and gets stuck, refusing new connections, if the previous one didn't end cleanly. Restart the game on the device (or re-apply RTSP mode in SysDVR Settings) to recover. “Test connection” always ends its session cleanly, so it won't cause this.

string.name: guide_rtsp_tip
string.value: Unless you specifically need RTSP, use TCP Bridge — it's smoother and uses less bandwidth on the same network.

string.name: guide_opt_title
string.value: Options explained

string.name: guide_opt_intro
string.value: All options live on the Settings tab, with tags showing which modes they apply to. During playback you can also change them instantly via “Settings” at the top right.

string.name: guide_opt_audio_title
string.value: Play sound

string.name: guide_opt_audio_body
string.value: In TCP Bridge, turning it off makes the device stop sending audio, saving about 1.5 Mbps for smoother video on a weak network. In USB and RTSP it simply mutes locally.

string.name: guide_opt_smooth_title
string.value: Smoothing

string.name: guide_opt_smooth_body
string.value: Trades a little buffering for smoothness when the network jitters. Off: no extra buffering, lower latency. Low latency: ≤80 ms buffer, for playing yourself and action games. Smoothness: ≤300 ms buffer, smoother, for watching story scenes or streams. “Low latency” is on by default — turn it off for even lower latency in rhythm or fighting games, or switch to “Smoothness” if it still stutters. The buffer adapts to the actual jitter and audio stays in sync.

string.name: guide_opt_net_title
string.value: Network optimization

string.name: guide_opt_net_body
string.value: Enables TCP quick ACK and uses Huawei Network Boost to mark the stream as real-time gaming with high-priority connections. TCP Bridge only.

string.name: guide_opt_hotspot_title
string.value: Device hotspot

string.name: guide_opt_hotspot_body
string.value: Creates a 5 GHz hotspot the device can see, in one tap. Once it's on, tap “Hotspot settings” to view or customize the network name and password (they're remembered, so the device reconnects automatically next time), and optionally start the hotspot whenever the app opens.

string.name: guide_opt_screen_title
string.value: Turn off device screen while streaming

string.name: guide_opt_screen_body
string.value: Turns the device screen off during streaming to save power and reduce heat; it comes back on when you disconnect. Requires SysDVR 6.0 or later (protocol 03).

string.name: guide_opt_keep_title
string.value: Keep alive in background

string.name: guide_opt_keep_body
string.value: In the background the app keeps receiving without rendering and shows a Live View in the notification panel (swipe it away to stop). The picture is back within a second when you return. It disconnects automatically after the chosen time.

string.name: guide_opt_stats_title
string.value: Show statistics

string.name: guide_opt_stats_body
string.value: Shows received/displayed frame rate, bitrate, dropped frames, audio buffer and underruns (off by default). “Received” below 30 means the network is the bottleneck; normal “received” but low “displayed” points to this phone or tablet; both at 0 means the device isn't sending video (e.g. the game blocks recording).

string.name: guide_opt_lock_title
string.value: Screen lock during playback

string.name: guide_opt_lock_body
string.value: During playback, tap the picture to show or hide the controls. Tap the lock icon on the left to lock the screen: only the lock icon remains, and back gestures or accidental taps won't disconnect. Tap the lock icon again to unlock.

string.name: guide_opt_dark_title
string.value: Dark mode

string.name: guide_opt_dark_body
string.value: In Settings → Other settings, follow the system or choose light or dark just for this app.

string.name: guide_opt_lang_title
string.value: Language

string.name: guide_opt_lang_body
string.value: In Settings → Other settings, follow the system language or choose 简体中文, 繁體中文 or English.

string.name: guide_faq_title
string.value: FAQ

string.name: guide_faq_q1
string.value: Connected but the screen is black

string.name: guide_faq_a1
string.value: The current game or system menu blocks recording — try another game. Or the mode on the device doesn't match the one selected in this app.

string.name: guide_faq_q2
string.value: Stuttering or low frame rate

string.name: guide_faq_a2
string.value: Turn on statistics and check the “received” frame rate. Below 30 means the network can't keep up — switch to the device hotspot or USB. Turning off sound saves bandwidth; for occasional drops, switch Smoothing to “Smoothness” (the default is “Low latency”).

string.name: guide_faq_q3
string.value: Choppy audio

string.name: guide_faq_a3
string.value: Usually caused by network jitter. Smoothing (on by default) also enlarges the audio buffer; if it still cuts out, try “Smoothness”, or turn sound off and just watch.

string.name: guide_faq_q4
string.value: Device not found

string.name: guide_faq_a4
string.value: Make sure the device and phone are on the same network and not on a guest network. You can also enter the device's IP directly (see System Settings → Internet → Connection Status on the device).

string.name: guide_faq_q5
string.value: Disconnected after turning off WLAN

string.name: guide_faq_a5
string.value: The device hotspot relies on WLAN, so turning WLAN off also turns off the hotspot. This is expected.

string.name: guide_opt_freeze_title
string.value: Freeze on frame loss

string.name: guide_opt_freeze_body
string.value: When the network stalls, the device drops frames it can't send in time, and the frames after them lack references and look corrupted until the next keyframe. With this on (the default), playback holds the last intact frame and resumes at the next keyframe, turning corruption into a brief pause; if no keyframe arrives within 3 seconds it plays on. With it off, playback never pauses but may show corruption. The “Loss” and “Freezes” lines in the statistics show how often this happens.

string.name: guide_opt_enhance_title
string.value: Picture enhancement

string.name: guide_opt_enhance_body
string.value: The device outputs 720p, which looks soft when stretched to a high-resolution screen. This uses the system's video detail enhancement to upscale to the resolution actually shown on screen and sharpen details, most noticeable on tablets and PCs. Standard is fast with low latency; High looks better but takes longer per frame and uses more power. Changing it during playback refreshes the picture once. Some devices (such as emulators) don't support it; the app then falls back to direct output and tells you why.
